description.value: The study examined large-scale network functional connectivity differences during distraction and reappraisal in healthy participants and remitted bipolar and unipolar disorder patients.

value: We hypothesized that the focus on an external cognitive task (i.e. arithmetic task) during distraction will induce anti-correlations between the DMN and cognitive control networks and enhanced connectivity among the cognitive control networks.

On the other hand, increased functional connectivity between cognitive control networks and DMN may be essential for the successful implementation of the initial appraisal and reappraisal of the situation.
Based on this evidence, we hypothesized that remitted UD and BD patients also exhibit a functional imbalance between the DMN and cognitive control networks during distraction and reappraisal.
